info.title: Perfect Venue REST API Docs
info.description:
# Introduction

Welcome to the Perfect Venue API docs. Customers on the Enterprise plan can create their own apps
from Settings in Perfect Venue; see [Creating an app](#section/Authentication/Creating-an-app).
Partners building an integration for many customers should reach out to support@perfectvenue.com
and we'll help you get set up.


This site was generated with [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/Redoc) and the [OpenAPI/Swagger
format](https://github.com/OAI/OpenAPI-Specification/blob/main/versions/3.0.2.md).

# Quick start

Use this flow when building a new integration:

  1. Create an app under **Settings → Developer** in Perfect Venue (Enterprise plan), or contact
     support@perfectvenue.com if you are a partner building for many customers. See
     [Creating an app](#section/Authentication/Creating-an-app).
  2. Copy the app's client ID and client secret to your server.
  3. Send a Perfect Venue user with access to the relevant venues through the OAuth authorization code flow, requesting the [scopes](#section/Authentication/Scopes) you need.
  4. Exchange the authorization code for an access token and refresh token.
  5. Call `GET /venues` to find the venues available to the authorizing Perfect Venue user.
  6. Store the Perfect Venue `venue_id` values in your system.
  7. Create events with `POST /events`, including contact details inline when you do not already have a `contact_id`.
  8. Use `GET /events` plus webhooks to keep your system in sync.

All authenticated API requests use this base URL:

~~~
https://api.perfectvenue.com/api/v1
~~~

# Implementation path

**1. List venues**

After a Perfect Venue user authorizes your integration, call `GET /venues` first. Venue IDs are required when creating events.
The venue response also includes venue-specific configuration such as event types, spaces, and custom fields.

~~~
curl https://api.perfectvenue.com/api/v1/venues \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN"
~~~

Save the `id` for each venue your integration should write to. We recommend mapping each
Perfect Venue `venue_id` to the equivalent resource in your system, such as a location,
merchant, store, or account.

**2. Create an event**

Create an event with a known `contact_id`, or pass a top-level `contact` object to create or reuse a contact
inline. Use `start_time` and `end_time` for new integrations; `start_date` and `end_date` are deprecated.

~~~
curl https://api.perfectvenue.com/api/v1/events \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "event": {
      "venue_id": "VENUE_ID",
      "name": "Henry's Wedding",
      "start_time": "2026-08-15T18:00:00Z",
      "end_time": "2026-08-15T23:00:00Z",
      "group_size": 120,
      "source": "Partner Integration",
      "event_type": "Wedding",
      "spaces": ["main-hall"],
      "custom": {
        "dietary_restrictions": "vegan"
      }
    },
    "contact": {
      "first_name": "Ada",
      "last_name": "Lovelace",
      "email": "ada@example.com",
      "phone": "+14155550100"
    },
    "message": {
      "text": "Interested in a Saturday evening reception."
    }
  }'
~~~

**3. Sync events**

Use `GET /events` to backfill or reconcile data. Always pass `venue_id`; use pagination for large result sets.

~~~
curl "https://api.perfectvenue.com/api/v1/events?venue_id=VENUE_ID&per_page=100&page=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN"
~~~

For incremental syncs, filter by `updated_at`:

~~~
curl "https://api.perfectvenue.com/api/v1/events?venue_id=VENUE_ID&date_field=updated_at&date_from=2026-06-01T00:00:00Z&date_to=2026-06-30T23:59:59Z" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN"
~~~

# Data model notes

  * `venue_id` identifies a venue available to the authorizing Perfect Venue user and is required for creating contacts and events.
  * `contact_id` identifies the event's primary contact.
  * `event_type` must match an event type configured for the venue.
  * `spaces` should contain space slugs from the venue's `spaces` array.
  * `custom` values are keyed by the venue's custom field `key`.
  * Event timestamps are ISO 8601 strings. Use the venue's `timezone` when displaying local times to users.
  * Money amounts are integer cents, for example `150000` for $1,500.00.

# Versioning

Send a `PV-Version` header to choose the response format. Without it, every endpoint keeps the
default format it has always returned, so existing integrations don't change. New integrations
should send the latest version.

~~~
curl https://api.perfectvenue.com/api/v1/venues \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "PV-Version: 2026-11-01"
~~~

| Version | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Default (no header) | Successful responses are `{"status": "success", "data": ...}`. Errors use the formats in [Error handling](#section/Error-handling). |
| `2026-11-01` | Successful responses are `{"data": ...}`, with list paging in a top level `meta`. Every error is a problem details body with a `request_id`. [List contacts](#tag/Contacts/operation/listContacts) is available. |

The response echoes the version you sent in a `PV-Version` header. An unknown version returns
`400 Bad Request` naming the supported versions.

# Error handling

Under `PV-Version: 2026-11-01`, every error uses the problem details format
([RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457)). Branch on `type`, which stays the same
when the wording of `detail` changes.

~~~json
{
  "type": "https://docs.perfectvenue.com/api/errors/not-found",
  "title": "Not found",
  "status": 404,
  "detail": "Venue not found",
  "request_id": "9f6c2b0e-4a1d-4c55-8a3e-2f7d1c9b6a10"
}
~~~

Some validation errors also include `errors`, an array of `field`, `code`, and `message`.

| `type` ends with | Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid-request` | 400 | A parameter is missing or invalid, or `PV-Version` is unknown |
| `validation-error` | 400 | The record failed validation |
| `authentication-error` | 401 | The access token is missing, invalid, expired, or revoked |
| `insufficient-scope` | 403 | The token is missing a required [scope](#section/Authentication/Scopes) |
| `forbidden` | 403 | The authorizing user can't access the venue or resource |
| `not-found` | 404 | The resource doesn't exist or isn't visible to the authorizing user |
| `internal-error` | 500 | Something went wrong on our side |

Without `PV-Version`, most errors use `status: "fail"` with messages in `data.errors`:

~~~json
{
  "status": "fail",
  "data": {
    "errors": [
      { "message": "End time must be after start time" }
    ]
  }
}
~~~

In the default format, a missing, invalid, or expired token returns `401` with an empty body.
The reason is in the `WWW-Authenticate` header, for example
`Bearer realm="Doorkeeper", error="invalid_token", error_description="The access token is invalid"`.
A missing scope on an application created before 2026-11-01 returns `403` with an empty body,
except from the team member endpoints.
Other missing scopes return the `status: "fail"` body with `code: "insufficient_scope"`. Unexpected server errors return
`{"status": "error", "message": "Internal server error"}`.

Rate limited requests return `429 Too Many Requests` with a problem details body in every
version. See [Rate limiting](#section/Rate-limiting).

# Request IDs

Every response has an `X-Request-Id` header. Problem details bodies, including rate limit
responses, repeat it as `request_id`. Log it with failed requests and include it when you contact
support@perfectvenue.com, so we can find the request.

# Authentication

The Perfect Venue API uses OAuth 2.0 Bearer tokens for authentication. Partner developers build
and operate integrations, but a Perfect Venue user must log in and authorize the application
before the integration can access venue data.

At a high level:

  1. Perfect Venue provisions an OAuth application for your integration.
  2. Your integration redirects a Perfect Venue user to the authorization URL.
  3. The user logs in and grants permission.
  4. Perfect Venue redirects the user back to your `redirect_uri` with an authorization code.
  5. Your server exchanges that code for an access token and refresh token.
  6. Your integration uses the access token when calling the API.

Access is limited to the Perfect Venue user who authorized the application. For example, if that
user can access two venues, `GET /venues` returns those venues and API writes are limited to
resources that user can access.

## Creating an app

An app is what connects your software, or a tool you use, to Perfect Venue on behalf of a
team. Organization admins on the Enterprise plan create apps themselves under
**Settings → Developer** at `app.perfectvenue.com/settings/developer`. Organizations on other
plans keep managing the apps they already have, and partners building for many customers can
ask support@perfectvenue.com to set one up.

When you create an app you choose:

| Field | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Name and logo | Shown to people on the consent screen when they connect the app |
| Redirect URIs | One per line. Must use `https`; `localhost` and `http` are not accepted |
| Private | Only your own organization can connect a private app. This cannot be changed after the app is created |

A **private** app is ready to use as soon as it is created, and its tokens only ever reach
venues in your organization. A **public** app is reviewed by Perfect Venue before other
organizations can connect it; until it is approved, you can connect and test it from your own
account. Changing a published app's name, logo, or redirect URIs sends it back to review, and
other organizations cannot connect it until it is approved again.

## OAuth credentials

Each app has the following values, shown on the Developer settings page or provided by Perfect
Venue during setup:

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `client_id` | Public identifier for your OAuth application |
| `client_secret` | Secret used by your server when exchanging authorization codes and refresh tokens |
| `redirect_uri` | Callback URL registered for your integration |

Keep the `client_secret` on your server. Do not expose it in browser code, mobile apps, logs,
or customer-visible configuration.

## Authorizing the app

Direct a Perfect Venue user to the Authorization URL with the following query parameters. The user must log in
and grant permission before your integration can receive an authorization code.

  * `response_type`: Set to "code"
  * `client_id`: Your application's unique client ID, provided by Perfect Venue
  * `redirect_uri`: The URL to which the user will be redirected after authorization
  * `scope`: Space separated [scopes](#section/Authentication/Scopes) your integration needs, for example `public read write`. Leave it out to request only `public`.
  * `state`: (Optional but recommended) A random string to maintain state between the request and callback, helping to prevent [CSRF attacks](https://auth0.com/docs/secure/attack-protection/state-parameters)

Example Authorization URL:

~~~
  https://api.perfectvenue.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&scope=public%20read%20write&state=RANDOM_STRING
~~~ 

Always validate the `state` value on the callback before exchanging the authorization code.

## Obtaining an access token

Once the Perfect Venue user has authorized your application, they will be redirected to the specified
`redirect_uri` with a `code` parameter in the query string. If authorization fails or the user
declines access, the redirect may include an OAuth error instead of `code`.


To exchange this authorization code for an access token, send a POST request to the Token URL
with the following setup:

  1. `Authorization` Header: Use Basic HTTP authentication, where the `client_id` and `client_secret` are
  combined in the format `client_id:client_secret` and Base64 encoded. This encoded value is included in the
  Authorization header as `Basic <encoded_credentials>`.
  2. Body Parameters (URL-encoded)  
      * `grant_type`: Set to "authorization_code"
      * `code`: The authorization code received in the redirect
      * `redirect_uri`: Must match the `redirect_uri` used the previous step


Example Token Request:  

~~~
  POST https://api.perfectvenue.com/oauth/token
  Authorization: Basic BASE64_ENCODED(client_id:client_secret)
  Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

  grant_type=authorization_code&code=AUTHORIZATION_CODE&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI
~~~

Example Token Response:

~~~json
{
  "access_token": "ACCESS_TOKEN",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 7200,
  "refresh_token": "REFRESH_TOKEN",
  "scope": "public read write",
  "created_at": 1782950400
}
~~~

Store tokens securely. Access tokens last 2 hours (`expires_in` is in seconds). Refresh tokens
should be treated like passwords because they can be exchanged for new access tokens.

## Scopes

The user sees the scopes you request on the consent screen, and the access token can only do
what they cover. Request the smallest set your integration needs.

| Scope | Grants | Consent screen text |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `public` | The default scope, granted to every token | Perfect Venue public API access |
| `read` | Reading venues, events, and contacts | View your venues, events, and contacts |
| `write` | Creating and updating events and contacts | Create and update your events and contacts |
| `contacts_read` | [List contacts](#tag/Contacts/operation/listContacts) | Contacts name and email |
| `users_read` | [List team members](#tag/Users/operation/listUsers) and [Get team member](#tag/Users/operation/getUser) | Names, roles, and email addresses of your team members |

`read` and `write` are separate: a token with only `write` can't read. Applications created
before 2026-11-01 don't need `read` or `write`; their `public` tokens keep working for venues,
events, and contacts.

A request with a token that lacks the scope returns `403 Forbidden`, and the body names the
missing scope. The exception is an application created before 2026-11-01 that doesn't send
`PV-Version`: it gets an empty `403` body, except from the team member endpoints.

## Using access tokens

Upon a successful token exchange, you’ll receive a JSON response with an access token.
Include this token in the Authorization header as `Bearer <token>` for all authenticated requests.  

Access tokens represent the Perfect Venue user who authorized the application. API responses and writes
are limited to the venues and resources that user can access in Perfect Venue.


Example API Request:

~~~
  GET /api/v1/venues
  Host: api.perfectvenue.com
  Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN
~~~

## Using refresh tokens

Token responses will include a refresh token that can be exchanged for a new access token.

To exchange a refresh token for a new access token, send a POST request to the Token URL
with the following setup:

  1. `Authorization` Header: Use Basic HTTP authentication, where the `client_id` and `client_secret` are
  combined in the format `client_id:client_secret` and Base64 encoded. This encoded value is included in the
  Authorization header as `Basic <encoded_credentials>`.
  2. Body Parameters (URL-encoded)  
      * `grant_type`: Set to "refresh_token"
      * `refresh_token`: The refresh token obtained from a previous token request
  
Example Refresh Token Request:  

~~~
  POST https://api.perfectvenue.com/oauth/token
  Authorization: Basic BASE64_ENCODED(client_id:client_secret)
  Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

  grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=REFRESH_TOKEN
~~~

Your integration should refresh the token before it expires or when an API request returns
`401 Unauthorized` because the access token is expired. If a refresh request fails, send the
Perfect Venue user through the authorization flow again.

Each refresh returns a new refresh token as well as a new access token, with the same scopes.
Store the new refresh token. The previous one stops working once you use the new access token.
Refresh tokens don't expire on their own; they stop working when revoked.

## Revoking tokens

Use token revocation when a user disconnects your integration, when you rotate stored
credentials, or when you no longer need access for a Perfect Venue user.

Send a `POST` request to the revocation endpoint with client authentication and the token you
want to revoke:

~~~
  POST https://api.perfectvenue.com/oauth/revoke
  Authorization: Basic BASE64_ENCODED(client_id:client_secret)
  Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

  token=ACCESS_OR_REFRESH_TOKEN
~~~

Request parameters:

| Parameter | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `token` | Yes | Access token or refresh token to revoke |
| `token_type_hint` | No | Optional hint such as `access_token` or `refresh_token` |

Successful revocation returns `200 OK` with an empty JSON body. The endpoint also returns
`200 OK` for missing, invalid, or already revoked tokens. If the token was issued to a
different OAuth client, Perfect Venue returns `403 Forbidden` with `unauthorized_client`.

After revoking a token, remove it from your system. If your integration needs access again,
send the Perfect Venue user through the OAuth authorization flow to receive new tokens.

## Authentication errors

| Status | Meaning | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401 Unauthorized` | The access token is missing, invalid, expired, or revoked | Refresh the token or send the user through OAuth again |
| `403 Forbidden` | The token is valid, but the authorizing user does not have access to the requested venue or resource | Ask the user to confirm their Perfect Venue permissions or authorize with a different user |
| `403 Forbidden` (missing scope) | The token doesn't have a scope the endpoint requires; the body names it, unless an application created before 2026-11-01 omits `PV-Version` (then the body is empty, except from the team member endpoints) | Send the user through OAuth again, requesting that scope |

# Rate limiting

The API is rate limited to **100 requests per minute per access token**. If you exceed this
limit, the API will respond with `429 Too Many Requests`.

When a request is rate limited, the response includes headers that help you decide when to retry:

| Header | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Retry-After` | Seconds to wait before retrying |
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Maximum requests allowed per minute |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | Requests remaining in the current window |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | Unix timestamp when the current limit window resets |

The `429` body is a problem details object in every version, with a `request_id`:

~~~json
{
  "type": "https://docs.perfectvenue.com/lead-form-api/errors/rate-limited",
  "title": "Rate limit exceeded",
  "status": 429,
  "detail": "You have exceeded 100 requests per minute. Try again in 42 seconds.",
  "request_id": "9f6c2b0e-4a1d-4c55-8a3e-2f7d1c9b6a10"
}
~~~

When you receive a `429`, wait before retrying. For API support, contact support@perfectvenue.com.

tags.name: Proposals
tags.description:
A proposal is what a venue sends a planner to agree to: the line items, prices, policies, and
signature for an event. Most events have one proposal; venues on the Enterprise plan can send
several alternatives for the same event.

Every event returned by the Events endpoints carries its proposals in a `proposals` array, so
syncing events gives you their documents with no extra requests. Use
[Get proposal](#tag/Proposals/operation/getProposal) when you have a proposal ID on its own, for
example from the `proposal.signed` webhook. Webhook event payloads do not include `proposals`.

Every proposal lists the documents Perfect Venue can produce for it, such as the BEO, Staff BEO,
invoice, event summary, guest menu, floor plans, and the venue's custom documents, each with a
link to the PDF. The PDF is rendered from the proposal's current contents when the link is opened.
These are the same links the Perfect Venue app uses and they open without authentication today;
a future version may require a Perfect Venue login, and this changelog will say so in advance.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Perfect Venue can notify your application in real time when data changes for venues available
to the authorizing Perfect Venue user. Use webhooks for incremental updates, and use the REST API to
fetch the current resource state whenever you need to reconcile.

**Quick start**

Use this flow when adding webhook support:

1. Build an HTTPS endpoint that can receive `POST` requests from Perfect Venue.
2. Send Perfect Venue your endpoint URL and the event types your integration needs.
3. Perfect Venue will add the webhook endpoint and event subscriptions to your OAuth application.
4. Store the endpoint signing secret provided during setup.
5. Verify the `PV-Signature` header on every delivery.
6. Use `PV-Webhook-Id` as your idempotency key.
7. Return a `2xx` response only after you have safely accepted the delivery.
8. Fetch the latest resource from the REST API when your local copy needs reconciliation.

**Subscribing to events**

Webhook subscriptions are configured by Perfect Venue; the Developer settings page does not
manage them yet. To subscribe, send support@perfectvenue.com:

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Endpoint URL | The HTTPS URL where Perfect Venue should send webhook deliveries |
| Event types | One or more public event type names from the table below |
| OAuth application | The OAuth application Perfect Venue configured for your integration |

Example setup request:

```text
Endpoint URL: https://example.com/perfect-venue/webhooks
Event types: event.created, event.status_changed, event.deleted, contact.created, proposal.signed, payment.succeeded
OAuth application: Partner Integration Name
```

Perfect Venue configures webhook subscriptions on your OAuth application. Your endpoint can
subscribe to multiple event types.

Your endpoint must be reachable over HTTPS and should be prepared to receive duplicate
deliveries.

Your endpoint receives events only for venues available to users who have authorized your OAuth application.

**Delivery request**

Each delivery is an HTTPS `POST` to your configured endpoint.

Required headers:

| Header | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `Content-Type` | Always `application/json` |
| `PV-Webhook-Id` | Stable delivery ID. Use this to deduplicate retries. |
| `PV-Signature` | Timestamped HMAC signature used to verify the request. |

Example delivery:

```http
POST /perfect-venue/webhooks HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
PV-Webhook-Id: f8c1a0e2-6d2f-4a0d-99a2-1fd6f9f3c1aa
PV-Signature: t=1718557200,v1=5257a869e7ecebeda32affa62cdca3fa...
```

**Payload envelope**

The JSON body always follows this envelope:

```json
{
  "id": "f8c1a0e2-6d2f-4a0d-99a2-1fd6f9f3c1aa",
  "type": "event.created",
  "api_version": "2026-06-01",
  "created_at": "2026-06-16T17:00:00Z",
  "data": {
    "id": "dfa4b137-1b3e-4927-a3d8-0e0e5bd601e3",
    "venue_id": "VENUE_ID",
    "contact_id": "CONTACT_ID",
    "owner_id": "user_8xZk2LmQp4Vd7A",
    "name": "Henry's Wedding",
    "status": "lead",
    "start_date": "2026-08-15T18:00:00Z",
    "end_date": "2026-08-15T23:00:00Z",
    "start_time": "2026-08-15T18:00:00Z",
    "end_time": "2026-08-15T23:00:00Z",
    "event_type": "Wedding",
    "spaces": ["main-hall"],
    "created_at": "2026-06-16T17:00:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-06-16T17:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

The `data` object contains the payload for the specific event type.

**Event types**

| Type | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `event.created` | An event (booking or lead) is created |
| `event.status_changed` | An event's status changes; payload includes the previous status |
| `event.deleted` | An event is deleted (soft deleted) |
| `contact.created` | A new inbound inquiry arrives |
| `proposal.signed` | A planner signs a proposal |
| `payment.succeeded` | A payment is marked paid |

**Payloads**

**`event.created` and `event.deleted`**

The `data` payload is the Event object — the same shape returned by
[Get Event](#tag/Events/operation/getEvent) and [List Events](#tag/Events/operation/listEvents).

Example `event.created` payload:

```json
{
  "id": "f8c1a0e2-6d2f-4a0d-99a2-1fd6f9f3c1aa",
  "type": "event.created",
  "api_version": "2026-06-01",
  "created_at": "2026-06-16T17:00:00Z",
  "data": {
    "id": "dfa4b137-1b3e-4927-a3d8-0e0e5bd601e3",
    "venue_id": "VENUE_ID",
    "contact_id": "CONTACT_ID",
    "owner_id": "user_8xZk2LmQp4Vd7A",
    "name": "Henry's Wedding",
    "status": "lead",
    "start_date": "2026-08-15T18:00:00Z",
    "end_date": "2026-08-15T23:00:00Z",
    "start_time": "2026-08-15T18:00:00Z",
    "end_time": "2026-08-15T23:00:00Z",
    "group_size": 120,
    "source": "Partner Integration",
    "campaign": "Summer 2026",
    "amount": 150000,
    "event_type": "Wedding",
    "spaces": ["main-hall"],
    "created_at": "2026-06-16T17:00:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-06-16T17:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

Example `event.deleted` payload:

```json
{
  "id": "9be6ab48-55f2-46f3-bd07-74af424c0f03",
  "type": "event.deleted",
  "api_version": "2026-06-01",
  "created_at": "2026-06-17T15:30:00Z",
  "data": {
    "id": "dfa4b137-1b3e-4927-a3d8-0e0e5bd601e3",
    "venue_id": "VENUE_ID",
    "contact_id": "CONTACT_ID",
    "owner_id": "user_8xZk2LmQp4Vd7A",
    "name": "Henry's Wedding",
    "status": "lost",
    "start_date": "2026-08-15T18:00:00Z",
    "end_date": "2026-08-15T23:00:00Z",
    "start_time": "2026-08-15T18:00:00Z",
    "end_time": "2026-08-15T23:00:00Z",
    "event_type": "Wedding",
    "spaces": ["main-hall"],
    "created_at": "2026-06-16T17:00:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-06-17T15:30:00Z"
  }
}
```

**`contact.created`**

The `data` payload is the Contact object — the same shape returned by
[Get Contact](#tag/Contacts/operation/getContact).

Only inbound inquiries emit this event.

Example `contact.created` payload:

```json
{
  "id": "7f6adfe6-9e01-4644-b850-3877b56526c8",
  "type": "contact.created",
  "api_version": "2026-06-01",
  "created_at": "2026-06-16T17:00:00Z",
  "data": {
    "id": "CONTACT_ID",
    "venue_id": "VENUE_ID",
    "first_name": "Ada",
    "last_name": "Lovelace",
    "email": "ada@example.com",
    "phone": "+14155550100"
  }
}
```

**`event.status_changed`**

A thin payload carrying only what changed. Use the `id` to fetch the full event from the
REST API if you need other fields.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Event ID |
| `venue_id` | string | Venue ID |
| `status` | string | New status |
| `previous_status` | string\|null | Status before the change |
| `updated_at` | string | ISO 8601 timestamp of the change |

Example:

```json
{
  "id": "f8c1a0e2-6d2f-4a0d-99a2-1fd6f9f3c1aa",
  "type": "event.status_changed",
  "api_version": "2026-06-01",
  "created_at": "2026-06-16T17:00:00Z",
  "data": {
    "id": "dfa4b137-1b3e-4927-a3d8-0e0e5bd601e3",
    "venue_id": "VENUE_ID",
    "status": "confirmed",
    "previous_status": "proposal_sent",
    "updated_at": "2026-06-16T17:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

**`proposal.signed`**

Sent when a planner signs a proposal. The signature itself is never included.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Proposal ID |
| `event_id` | string | Event ID, the same `id` the Events endpoints return |
| `venue_id` | string\|null | Venue ID |
| `action` | string\|null | What the proposal asks the planner to do: `agreement_deposit`, `agreement`, `deposit`, `remaining_balance`, `no_action`, `other_payment`, or `countersign` |
| `signed_at` | string\|null | ISO 8601 timestamp of the signature |
| `created_at` | string | ISO 8601 timestamp |
| `updated_at` | string | ISO 8601 timestamp |

Example:

```json
{
  "id": "0b9a5c1e-7d44-4f1e-9a63-2f4e8f0c7d21",
  "type": "proposal.signed",
  "api_version": "2026-06-01",
  "created_at": "2026-06-20T18:04:00Z",
  "data": {
    "id": "proposal_Qm3vX8kTz1LpRw",
    "event_id": "dfa4b137-1b3e-4927-a3d8-0e0e5bd601e3",
    "venue_id": "VENUE_ID",
    "action": "agreement_deposit",
    "signed_at": "2026-06-20T18:03:41Z",
    "created_at": "2026-06-18T16:00:00Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-06-20T18:03:41Z"
  }
}
```

**`payment.succeeded`**

Sent when a payment is marked paid, whatever the payment processor.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Payment ID |
| `event_id` | string | Event ID, the same `id` the Events endpoints return |
| `venue_id` | string | Venue ID |
| `amount` | integer | Amount in cents |
| `kind` | string | `deposit`, `remaining_balance`, or `other` |
| `state` | string | Payment state, `paid` |
| `mechanism` | string | `card`, `ach`, or `offline` |
| `paid_at` | string\|null | ISO 8601 timestamp of the payment |
| `created_at` | string | ISO 8601 timestamp |
| `updated_at` | string | ISO 8601 timestamp |

Example:

```json
{
  "id": "5c2f8e0a-1b6d-4c3e-8f7a-9d0e1c2b3a45",
  "type": "payment.succeeded",
  "api_version": "2026-06-01",
  "created_at": "2026-06-20T18:10:00Z",
  "data": {
    "id": "payment_Hc7nV2qWx9KdTs",
    "event_id": "dfa4b137-1b3e-4927-a3d8-0e0e5bd601e3",
    "venue_id": "VENUE_ID",
    "amount": 250000,
    "kind": "deposit",
    "state": "paid",
    "mechanism": "card",
    "paid_at": "2026-06-20T18:09:52Z",
    "created_at": "2026-06-20T18:09:30Z",
    "updated_at": "2026-06-20T18:09:52Z"
  }
}
```

**Signature verification**

Every delivery includes a `PV-Signature` header:

```
PV-Signature: t=1718557200,v1=5257a869e7ecebeda32affa62cdca3fa...
```

`t` is the Unix timestamp the request was signed. `v1` is the HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of
`"#{msg_id}.#{t}.#{raw_body}"` where `msg_id` is the value of the `PV-Webhook-Id` header,
computed with your endpoint's signing secret.

Verification steps:

1. Read the raw request body before parsing JSON.
2. Parse `t` and `v1` from `PV-Signature`.
3. Reject requests where `t` is too far from the current time. We recommend a 5-minute tolerance.
4. Build the signed payload as `PV-Webhook-Id + "." + t + "." + raw_body`.
5. Compute the HMAC-SHA256 hex digest with your endpoint signing secret.
6. Compare the computed digest to `v1` using a constant-time comparison.

Including `PV-Webhook-Id` in the signed content means a replay attack with a swapped webhook ID
will fail verification.

Example Node.js verifier:

```javascript
const crypto = require("crypto");

function verifyPerfectVenueWebhook({ rawBody, webhookId, signatureHeader, signingSecret }) {
  const parts = Object.fromEntries(
    signatureHeader.split(",").map((part) => part.split("="))
  );
  const timestamp = parts.t;
  const expected = parts.v1;

  const signedPayload = `${webhookId}.${timestamp}.${rawBody}`;
  const actual = crypto
    .createHmac("sha256", signingSecret)
    .update(signedPayload)
    .digest("hex");

  return crypto.timingSafeEqual(
    Buffer.from(actual, "hex"),
    Buffer.from(expected, "hex")
  );
}
```

**Idempotency**

The `PV-Webhook-Id` header (and the `id` field in the body) is a stable identifier for an
event delivery. It does not change across retries. Use it to deduplicate: if you have already
processed an `id`, acknowledge with 2xx and ignore the repeat.

Delivery is at-least-once. Your handler must be safe to run twice for the same `PV-Webhook-Id`.

**Response handling**

Return a `2xx` status after your endpoint has accepted the delivery. Any non-2xx response,
timeout, or connection error is treated as a failed delivery and retried.

Recommended handler behavior:

1. Verify the signature.
2. Check whether `PV-Webhook-Id` has already been processed.
3. Persist the delivery or enqueue work in your system.
4. Return `2xx`.
5. Process the event asynchronously when possible.

**Ordering and sync**

There is no global ordering guarantee. Deliveries are dispatched concurrently and can arrive
out of order. Events about the same resource carry a `created_at` you can order by, and you
can always read the current state from the REST API to reconcile. For high-confidence syncs,
combine webhooks with periodic `GET /events` backfills filtered by `updated_at`.

**Retries and endpoint health**

A failed delivery is retried up to 15 times with exponential backoff, which spreads the
retries over several days. Retries resend the payload exactly as it was first built.

After 20 failed deliveries in a row with no success in between, Perfect Venue disables the
endpoint so it stops receiving deliveries, and emails your application's owners. Once the
endpoint is healthy, it can be turned back on to resume new deliveries.

**Payload changes**

We may add fields to an event type's `data` at any time. Each addition raises that type's schema
version and is listed in the [Changelog](#tag/Changelog). Ignore fields you don't recognize. If
you validate deliveries against a copy of these schemas, allow additional properties, or a new
field will make valid deliveries fail your check.

Removing or renaming a field, or changing its type, only happens under a new `api_version`.

| Date | Event types | Schema version | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-10-21 | `event.created`, `event.deleted` | 2 | Added `owner_id`, the ID of the team member who owns the event, or `null` when it has no owner. Look the owner up with [Get team member](#tag/Users/operation/getUser), which needs the `users_read` scope. |

tags.name: Changelog
tags.description:
## 1.6.0 (2026-11-09)

### Proposals

**Proposals on events.** Every event from [List Events](#tag/Events/operation/listEvents),
[Get Event](#tag/Events/operation/getEvent), [Create Event](#tag/Events/operation/createEvent),
and [Update Event](#tag/Events/operation/updateEvent) now has a `proposals` array: each proposal's
ID, whether it has been signed, and links to its PDF documents (BEO, Staff BEO, invoice, event
summary, guest menu, floor plans, and the venue's custom documents). Webhook payloads are unchanged.

**New [Get proposal](#tag/Proposals/operation/getProposal) endpoint.** Fetch one proposal by the
ID the `proposals` array and the `proposal.signed` webhook carry.

### Apps

**Self-service apps for Enterprise customers.** Organization admins on the Enterprise plan can
create and manage their own OAuth apps under Settings → Developer, including private apps that
only their organization can connect. See [Creating an app](#section/Authentication/Creating-an-app).

### Support

**New contact address.** API questions now go to support@perfectvenue.com.

## 1.5.0 (2026-11-05)

### Webhooks

**New `proposal.signed` and `payment.succeeded` webhooks.** Sent when a planner signs a
proposal and when a payment is marked paid. Every ID in their payloads is a public ID string,
like the other event types and the REST API. See [Webhooks](#tag/Webhooks).

## 1.4.0 (2026-10-29)

### Versioning and errors

**New `PV-Version` header.** Send `PV-Version: 2026-11-01` to get `{"data": ...}` responses and
problem details errors on every endpoint. Requests without the header are unchanged. See
[Versioning](#section/Versioning).

**Request IDs.** Every response has an `X-Request-Id` header, and problem details bodies repeat
it as `request_id`. See [Request IDs](#section/Request-IDs).

**Error example fixed.** The default error format nests messages under `data.errors`. The
example in [Error handling](#section/Error-handling) used to show them directly under `data`.

### Authentication

**Scopes are enforced.** Applications created on or after 2026-11-01 need `read` to read venues,
events, and contacts and `write` to create or update events and contacts. Older applications are
unchanged. See [Scopes](#section/Authentication/Scopes).

**Refresh tokens rotate.** Each refresh returns a new refresh token; store it. See
[Using refresh tokens](#section/Authentication/Using-refresh-tokens).

### Contacts

**New [List contacts](#tag/Contacts/operation/listContacts) endpoint** for syncing every contact,
with `updated_after`, `created_after`, and cursor paging. Requires `PV-Version: 2026-11-01` and
the `contacts_read` scope.

### Users

**New [List team members](#tag/Users/operation/listUsers) and
[Get team member](#tag/Users/operation/getUser) endpoints**, with the new `users_read` scope.

### Events

**New `owner_id` field** on events in every response, and in the `event.created` and
`event.deleted` webhooks (schema version 2).

### Webhooks

Documented the retry schedule, automatic disabling, and the rules for payload changes. See
[Webhooks](#tag/Webhooks).

## 1.3.0 — 2026-06-18

### Webhooks

**New [Webhooks](#tag/Webhooks) section**

Outgoing webhooks are now available. Register an HTTPS endpoint on your OAuth application
and subscribe to the event types you care about. Perfect Venue will POST a signed JSON
payload to your endpoint whenever a subscribed event occurs.

Event types available in this release:

| Type | Fires when |
| --- | --- |
| `event.created` | An event is created |
| `event.status_changed` | An event's status changes |
| `event.deleted` | An event is deleted |
| `contact.created` | A new inbound inquiry arrives |

See the [Webhooks](#tag/Webhooks) section for the full delivery contract, payload schemas,
signature verification, and retry behavior.

### Events

**New [List Events](#tag/Events/operation/listEvents) endpoint**

`GET /events` is now available. Returns a paginated list of events for a venue with support for filtering
by status, event type, source, spaces, contact, and date range.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `venue_id` | string | **Required.** The ID of the venue |
| `status` | string[] | Filter by status: `lead`, `qualified`, `proposal_sent`, `confirmed`, `balance_due`, `completed`, `lost` |
| `event_type` | string[] | Filter by event type name |
| `source` | string[] | Filter by event source |
| `spaces` | string[] | Filter by space slug |
| `contact_id` | string | Filter by contact ID |
| `order` | string | Sort field: `created_at` (default), `updated_at`, `start_time`, `name` |
| `sort_direction` | string | `asc` or `desc` (default) |
| `date_from` | string | ISO 8601 start of date range (requires `date_to`) |
| `date_to` | string | ISO 8601 end of date range (requires `date_from`) |
| `date_field` | string | Date field for range filter: `created_at` (default), `updated_at`, `start_time` |
| `page` | integer | Page number (default: 1) |
| `per_page` | integer | Results per page, max 100 (default: 25) |

## 1.2.0 — 2026-04-01

### Venues

**New fields on [Get Venue](#tag/Venues/operation/getVenue) and [List Venues](#tag/Venues/operation/listVenues)**

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `event_types` | object[] | Event types configured for the venue, each with a `name` |
| `spaces` | object[] | Spaces available at the venue, each with `slug`, `name`, `standing`, and `seated` capacity |
| `custom_fields` | object[] | Custom fields configured for the venue, each with `key`, `name`, `data_type`, and optional `options` |

### Events

**New fields on [Create Event](#tag/Events/operation/createEvent) and [Update Event](#tag/Events/operation/updateEvent)**

The following optional fields are now supported:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `amount` | integer | Estimated event value in cents (e.g. `150000` for $1,500.00) |
| `event_type` | string | Event type name, must match a type configured for the venue |
| `spaces` | string[] | Space slugs to assign to the event |
| `custom` | object | Custom field values keyed by field key |

**Inline contact creation on [Create Event](#tag/Events/operation/createEvent)**

You can now create a contact inline when creating an event by passing a top-level `contact` object
instead of a `contact_id`. If a contact with the given email already exists in your organization, it
will be reused.

**Initial message on [Create Event](#tag/Events/operation/createEvent)**

You can now include an initial message from the contact to the venue when creating an event by passing
a top-level `message` object with a `text` field.

**New [Update Event](#tag/Events/operation/updateEvent) endpoint**

`PATCH /events/{event_id}` is now available. All fields are optional — only the fields you include
will be updated.

get.description:
List venues available to the Perfect Venue user who authorized your application. Perfect Venue provisions OAuth application access for partner developers during integration setup, but a Perfect Venue user must log in and grant permission before your integration can call the API.

Requires the `read` scope for applications created on or after 2026-11-01. See [Scopes](#section/Authentication/Scopes).

Get an individual venue by ID.

Requires the `read` scope for applications created on or after 2026-11-01. See [Scopes](#section/Authentication/Scopes).

Returns a paginated list of events for a venue. Requires a `venue_id` query parameter.

Results can be filtered by status, event type, source, spaces, contact, or date range, and sorted by a configurable field and direction.

Pagination uses `page` and `per_page` query parameters. `page` defaults to `1`; values below `1` are treated as `1`. `per_page` defaults to `25` and is clamped between `1` and `100`.

Pagination metadata has `current_page`, `per_page`, `total_count`, and `total_pages`. By default the events are in `data.events` and the metadata in `data.meta`. Under `PV-Version: 2026-11-01`, `data` is the array of events and the metadata is in a top level `meta`.

Requires the `read` scope for applications created on or after 2026-11-01. See [Scopes](#section/Authentication/Scopes).

Creates a new event in a venue. 

Creating an event requires a `venue_id`. You can get a list of available venues for the authorizing Perfect Venue user by calling the [list venues](/#tag/Venues/operation/listVenues) endpoint.  

Creating an event requires `venue_id`, `name`, and either an `event.contact_id` or a top-level `contact` object. `start_time` and `end_time` are optional, but recommended for events with a known schedule.
When you create a contact via the [create contact](/#tag/Contacts/operation/createContact) endpoint, you will get back a unique identifier for the contact that can be used to create events. You can also provide a top-level `contact` object to create or reuse a contact inline.


Requires the `write` scope for applications created on or after 2026-11-01. See [Scopes](#section/Authentication/Scopes).

get.description:
Get an individual proposal by ID. The ID is the same `id` found in an event's `proposals` array and carried by the `proposal.signed` webhook.

Requires the `read` scope for applications created on or after 2026-11-01. See [Scopes](#section/Authentication/Scopes).

Lists every contact in the authorizing user's organization, oldest `updated_at` first, so you can sync contacts into your system. Requires `PV-Version: 2026-11-01`; without the header this endpoint returns an older format that only covers the last 24 hours, kept for existing integrations.

To sync, store `updated_at` from the last contact you processed and pass it as `updated_after` on the next run. Follow `meta.next_cursor` until it is `null` to read every page. The contact you stored may come back again on the next run, so make your import safe to repeat.

Requires the `contacts_read` scope.

custom.description: Custom field values for the event, keyed by custom field key

ContactFirstName.description: The first name of the contact

ContactLastName.description: The last name of the contact

ContactPhone.description: The phone number of the contact

custom.description: Custom field values for the event, keyed by custom field key

SyncedContact.description: A contact in the contacts list, with timestamps for syncing

updated_at.description: Also changes when the contact's guest profile name, email, or phone changes

User.description: A member of the authorizing user's organization

id.description: The ID of the team member. Matches `owner_id` on events.

role.description: The member's role in the organization

venue_ids.description: IDs of the organization's venues this member belongs to that your application can reach

BadRequest.description: Bad Request. A parameter is missing or invalid, validation failed, or `PV-Version` is unknown.

Unauthorized.description: Unauthorized. The access token is missing, invalid, expired, or revoked. Without `PV-Version` the body is empty and the reason is in the `WWW-Authenticate` header.

WWW-Authenticate.description: The OAuth error, for example `Bearer realm="Doorkeeper", error="invalid_token", error_description="The access token is invalid"`

Forbidden.description: Forbidden. The token is missing a required [scope](#section/Authentication/Scopes), or the authorizing user can't access the venue or resource. Without `PV-Version`, a missing scope on an application created before 2026-11-01 returns `403` with an empty body, except from the team member endpoints.

NotFound.description: Not Found. The resource doesn't exist or isn't visible to the authorizing user.

TooManyRequests.description: Too Many Requests. The access token exceeded the [rate limit](#section/Rate-limiting).
